title: Canary safety tuning, signal taxonomy, and shadow-test harness follow-up
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Summary: After last week's staged model rollout that triggered an automatic rollback due to noisy latency spikes and metric drift, this ticket captures required follow-ups: update the canary signal taxonomy, harden the shadow-traffic test harness, tune rollback hysteresis, and add preflight checks to prevent false-positive auto-rollbacks. The goal is to reduce unnecessary rollbacks while preserving fast automatic mitigation for real degradations.

Context: On 2026-02-05 we rolled model v2026-02-c into production with a 10% canary. At ~04:12 UTC a subset of requests experienced 3x tail latency increases tied to KV cache eviction behavior under short-lived bursts. The rollout controller interpreted the spike as a sustained SLO violation and executed the automated rollback. Post-incident analysis shows that the signal had high variance, was correlated with a small client subset, and was amplified by insufficient smoothing in the canary controller.

Scope of work:
- Define a canary signal taxonomy (latency percentiles, error classes, functional correctness signals) and map sources of noise vs. true regressions.
- Implement per-signal smoothing & outlier rejection (rolling windows, trimmed mean, and percentile bootstrapping) in the rollout controller.
- Introduce target-aware rollback hysteresis: require N contiguous evaluation windows and a minimum request volume before auto-rollback.
- Harden shadow-test harness to run shadow traffic with synthetic repeatable traces, deterministic KV-cache warmup, and client-segmentation to identify correlated client groups.
- Add a preflight evaluation step that runs candidate models with mini A/B traffic plus synthetic edge-case prompts (from our eval corpus) before enabling canary.
- Integrate canary verdicts into Console: annotate rollout timeline with signal buckets, client cohorts, and synthetic-test outcomes.
- Update runbook and incident playbooks with new diagnosis checklist and rollback override guidance.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Canary controller accepts a signal taxonomy config and applies smoothing/outlier rules (unit + integration tests).
2) Rollout controller respects hysteresis policy and rejects low-volume/noisy rollbacks (verified by synthetic injection tests).
3) Shadow harness can replay customer segments with cache warmup and produce a deterministic metric baseline (demo to SRE + PM).
4) Console shows annotated canary timelines and enables quick rollback veto with justification fields.
5) Runbook updated and reviewed by SRE, PM, and Security; drill scheduled for next incident response practice.
